mainTopic: The girl conceived before her mother's גירות but born after it; whether a מוציא שם רע pays when the girl is an orphan or a קטנה; and the start of שילא's three cases of an accused נערה.
overview: The משנה taught that a girl whose mother converted while pregnant with her is stoned if she commits adultery as a נערה המאורסה. It also taught that a husband who falsely accuses her (מוציא שם רע) is not flogged and does not pay the one hundred סלע. ריש לקיש finds the source in the extra word ״וָמֵתָה״. The גמרא shows that this word includes her only for the death penalty, and that ״בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״ keeps out a girl both conceived and born before conversion. Then רבי יוסי בר חנינא rules that one who falsely accuses an orphan girl is exempt, because the money goes 'to the father of the girl.' A challenge from רבי יוסי הגלילי's teaching about a seduced orphan is answered: there she became an orphan only after the act. רבא disagrees with רבי יוסי בר חנינא and proves from the exclusion of converts that the accuser of an orphan must pay. ריש לקיש rules that the accuser of a קטנה is exempt, but רב אחא בר אבא's objection turns the spelling lesson around: the short spelling נער elsewhere includes even a קטנה. Finally שילא begins a ברייתא listing three cases of an accused נערה, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Where do we learn the משנה's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's ruling about the girl conceived before her mother's conversion and born after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the source of the משנה's rule. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ruled that a girl conceived before her mother converted, but born after, is stoned like a born Jewish girl. Normally these special laws apply only to a girl born fully Jewish, so the גמרא wants to know what פסוק includes her.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
From where do we know these things? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: Gemara: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: 'These matters' means the משנה's rule that a girl conceived before her mother converted but born after is stoned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that includes a girl conceived before conversion and born after it in the death penalty of a נערה המאורסה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the word 'that she die' includes her
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the extra word ״וָמֵתָה״ comes to include a girl conceived before her mother converted but born after.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: The פסוק says 'that she die.' This comes to include a girl whose conception was not in holiness but whose birth was in holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the question by pointing to the word ״וָמֵתָה״ in the פסוק about the girl who is stoned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already says 'they shall stone her with stones,' so 'that she die' seems extra. ריש לקיש uses that extra word as a רבוי to add one more girl to the death penalty: one conceived before her mother's גירות but born after.

keyTerms.meaning: To include (an extra word adds a case)
In holiness, meaning after the mother became Jewish

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
As the verse states: "that she die,"
to include one whose conception was not in sanctity
but whose birth was in sanctity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word ״וָמֵתָה״ includes a girl conceived before conversion and born after it in the death penalty.

steps.title: Then the husband should also get lashes and pay
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק treats her like a regular Jewish girl, the husband who falsely accuses her should also be flogged and pay one hundred סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he should also get lashes, and he should also pay the one hundred סלע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: if she counts as a Jewish girl for the death penalty, why does the משנה exempt the husband who falsely accuses her?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a husband who falsely accuses this girl (מוציא שם רע) is not flogged and does not pay the fine. The challenge is that if the פסוק fully includes her, all the laws of that section should apply to her, including the husband's punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: One hundred סלע, the fine of the מוציא שם רע

phrases.english: If so, let him also be flogged,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the husband who falsely accused her of adultery.

phrases.english: and let him also pay one hundred sela!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the result of ריש לקיש's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's רבוי from ״וָמֵתָה״ combined with the משנה's exemption of the husband.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the girl is included as a full Jewish girl, the husband's lashes and fine should apply too, contradicting the משנה.

steps.title: Included only for death, not for the fine
steps.stepSummary: The word ״וָמֵתָה״ itself shows she was included only for the death penalty, not for the fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'that she die': she was included for death, not for the fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the very word used to include her limits the inclusion to the death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״וָמֵתָה״ speaks about death, so the רבוי only adds her to the death penalty. It does not make her a full Jewish girl for the rest of the section, so the husband's קנס does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine set by the תורה

phrases.english: The verse states: "that she die" —
she was included for death but not for the fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא ״וָמֵתָה״ — לְמִיתָה נִתְרַבְּתָה וְלֹא לִקְנָס
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the רבוי to the subject of the word itself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבוי makes her a full Jewish girl for every law in the section.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word ״וָמֵתָה״ includes her only for the death penalty, not for the husband's fine.

steps.title: Maybe the word includes a girl conceived and born after conversion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the word might come to include a girl whose conception and birth were both after her mother converted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it comes to include a girl whose conception and birth were both in holiness?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's reading by offering a different girl the word could be including.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe ״וָמֵתָה״ only teaches that a girl conceived and born after her mother's conversion counts, and not the in-between case. If so, ריש לקיש's case would lose its source.

phrases.english: But say it comes to include one whose conception and birth were in sanctity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to ריש לקיש's reading from step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבוי could be referring to a girl fully conceived and born after conversion instead.

steps.title: That girl is already fully Jewish
steps.stepSummary: A girl conceived and born after conversion is a fully Jewish girl, so no extra word is needed for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: That girl is a full-fledged Jewish woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that such a girl needs no special inclusion, since she is plainly a regular Jewish girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A girl conceived and born after her mother converted is no different from any other Jewish girl. A רבוי would be wasted on her, so the word must be adding the in-between case.

phrases.english: That one is a full-fledged Jewish woman.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the suggested case needs no רבוי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word might include a girl conceived and born after conversion.
steps.terutzMaskana: Such a girl is already a full Jewish girl, so the word must be adding the in-between case.

steps.title: Maybe the word includes a girl conceived and born before conversion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks from the other side: maybe the word includes even a girl whose conception and birth were both before her mother converted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it comes to include a girl whose conception and birth were both not in holiness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש from the opposite direction, suggesting the word includes even more than he said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the word adds girls who are not plain Jewish girls, maybe it adds even a girl born before the conversion. That would make the death penalty apply more widely than the משנה said.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in holiness, meaning before the mother became Jewish

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵימָא לְרַבּוֹת הוֹרָתָהּ וְלֵידָתָהּ שֶׁלֹּא בִּקְדוּשָּׁה!
phrases.english: But say it comes to include one whose conception and birth were not in sanctity!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא לְרַבּוֹת הוֹרָתָהּ וְלֵידָתָהּ שֶׁלֹּא בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A challenge from the opposite side of step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The limit of the רבוי of ״וָמֵתָה״.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word could include even a girl conceived and born before conversion.

steps.title: The word 'in Israel' excludes her
steps.stepSummary: If even a girl born before conversion were included, the words ״בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״ in the same פסוק would have no purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does 'in Israel' accomplish?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the same פסוק says ״בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״, which limits the law to a girl who was born Jewish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״ shows the law is for a girl born into the Jewish people. So ״וָמֵתָה״ can stretch to a girl born after conversion, but ״בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״ blocks a girl born before it. Together the two words land exactly on ריש לקיש's case.
steps.whatToRemember: ״וָמֵתָה״ includes a girl conceived before conversion but born after, only for the death penalty, not for the fine. ״בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״ keeps out a girl both conceived and born before conversion.

phrases.english: If so, "in Israel" — what does it accomplish?
phrases.notes: From the same פסוק, דברים 22:21: 'for she has done a shameful act in Israel.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 and secures ריש לקיש's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Another word in the פסוק limits the רבוי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word might include even a girl conceived and born before conversion.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״ limits the law to a girl born Jewish, so she is excluded.

steps.title: One who falsely accuses an orphan girl is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא rules that one who falsely accuses an orphan girl is exempt, since the פסוק gives the money to her father and she has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: One who spreads a bad name about an orphan girl is exempt, as it says: 'And they shall give it to the father of the girl' — this leaves out one who has no father.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רבי יוסי בר חנינא gives a rule about the מוציא שם רע when the girl has no father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the fine is given 'to the father of the girl.' רבי יוסי בר חנינא reads this as a limit: the law applies only to a girl who has a father, so one who falsely accuses an orphan is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: One who spreads a bad name; a husband who falsely claims his wife was unfaithful

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע עַל הַיְּתוֹמָה פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: One who defames an orphan girl is exempt,
as it is stated: "and give them to the father of the young woman" —
excluding this one who has no father.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא: הַמּוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע עַל הַיְּתוֹמָה פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching on a related topic, the laws of the מוציא שם רע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who falsely accuses an orphan girl is exempt, learned from 'to the father of the girl.'

steps.title: A challenge from the seduced orphan in רבי יוסי הגלילי's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין challenges the idea that a girl with no father gets no fine. רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from the double words ״מָאֵן יְמָאֵן״ that even an orphan gets the fine of a מפתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין (some say רבי יוסי בר זבידא) objected: the פסוק says ״And if her father utterly refuses.″ This comes to include an orphan girl for the fine. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict the idea that a girl with no father loses the fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a מפתה (seducer) also speaks of the father, and its fine normally goes to the father. Yet רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from the doubled word ״מָאֵן יְמָאֵן״ that an orphan still gets the fine. So having no father does not seem to cancel the fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Utterly refuses (the doubled verb used for a דרשה)
A fixed fine set by the תורה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin raised an objection,
and some say it was Rabbi Yosei bar Zevida:
"And if her father utterly refuses" —
phrases.notes: שמות 22:16. This is the פסוק about a seducer (מפתה), not about false accusation.

phrases.english: this comes to include an orphan girl for the fine,
phrases.notes: The doubled word "refuse, refuse" is read as hinting at a second refuser: the orphan girl herself.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of step 9 that a girl without a father gets no fine.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי בר חנינא's logic that, since the money goes to the father, an orphan has no fine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the parallel case of a מפתה, where the fine also goes to the father, a ברייתא gives the fine to an orphan anyway.

steps.title: The same רבי answers: she was orphaned after the act
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין answers his own challenge. רבי יוסי הגלילי means a girl whose father was alive at the time of the act and who became an orphan afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised the objection and he answered it: it is talking about a case where the man was with her, and only afterward she became an orphan.
steps.whatsHappening: The same רבי who asked the question now answers it by narrowing the case of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fine becomes owed at the moment of the act. If her father was alive then, the obligation already started, and his later death does not cancel it. A girl who was an orphan before the act is a different case, so step 9's ruling still stands.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ:
phrases.english: He raised the objection and he resolved it:
it refers to where he had relations with her, and afterward she was orphaned.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא gives the fine even to a girl who was an orphan when the act happened.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only about a girl whose father was alive at the time of the act, so it does not contradict step 9.

steps.title: רבא rules that the false accuser of an orphan must pay
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with רבי יוסי בר חנינא and says the one who falsely accuses an orphan girl is obligated to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite ruling from step 9: the false accuser of an orphan does pay. The next step brings his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בר חנינא exempted him because the פסוק gives the money to the father. רבא holds that the lack of a father does not remove the obligation.

phrases.english: Rava said: He is obligated.
phrases.notes: He is answering the case from step 9: someone who falsely accuses an orphan girl.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues against the ruling of רבי יוסי בר חנינא in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who falsely accuses an orphan girl must pay the fine.

steps.title: רבא's proof: the פסוק needed to exclude converts
steps.stepSummary: אמי taught that the fine is for ״a virgin of Israel″ and not for a convert. רבא argues that this exclusion only makes sense if a Jewish-born girl with no father is still owed the fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? From what אמי taught: ״a virgin of Israel,″ and not a virgin who is a convert. If you say that in such a case (no father) a Jewish-born girl gets the fine, then we understand why the פסוק needed to exclude converts. But if you say that in such a case a Jewish-born girl gets nothing, then if even a Jewish-born girl gets nothing, do we really need a פסוק for converts?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves his ruling: the פסוק bothers to exclude converts, so Jewish-born girls without a father must be included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A convert is treated like a girl with no father, because her family tie to her parents is cut off when she converts. If a Jewish-born orphan were already exempt, the convert would obviously be exempt too, and the פסוק would not need to say so. Since the פסוק does exclude converts, a Jewish-born orphan must be owed the fine.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא: the false accuser of an orphan pays. The proof is that the פסוק excludes converts. That exclusion would be pointless if Jewish-born girls with no father were already exempt.
steps.confusionAlert: The convert in אמי's teaching stands for a girl with no father. Without that point, רבא's proof will not make sense.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a clear argument between רבא and רבי יוסי בר חנינא over whether the father's absence cancels the fine.

phrases.english: From where? From what Ami taught:
"A virgin of Israel," and not a virgin who is a convert.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא
phrases.english: It works well if you say that in a case like this
phrases.notes: "A case like this" means a girl who has no father.

phrases.english: with a Jewish-born girl he is obligated;
that is why the verse was needed to exclude converts.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּהַאי גַוְונָא פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: But if you say that with a Jewish-born girl in a case like this he is exempt,
now, if with a Jewish-born girl he is exempt,
is it even necessary to say so for converts?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and reasoning for רבא's ruling in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that the false accuser of an orphan girl is obligated.
steps.raayaSupportSource: אמי's ברייתא: ״בְּתוּלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל״ and not a convert. The extra exclusion shows that Jewish-born girls without a father are included.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: no fine for falsely accusing a minor
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that a מוציא שם רע against a קטנה is פטור, because the פסוק spells ״נערה״ in full.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Someone who falsely accuses a young girl (a קטנה) is exempt. The פסוק says "give it to the father of the נערה," and here the word נערה is spelled in full. That shows the תורה means a girl who is fully a נערה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from ריש לקיש. The fine for falsely accusing a girl does not apply if she is a קטנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this פרשה the word נערה is usually written without the final ה. In the payment פסוק it is spelled with the ה, and ריש לקיש reads this as "a full נערה," which leaves out a קטנה. So a קטנה gets no fine.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl under twelve, before she is a נערה
A girl from about twelve until six months later, when she becomes a בוגרת
Spelled in full, with all its letters

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע עַל הַקְּטַנָּה — פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: One who defames a minor girl is exempt,
as it is said: "And they shall give to the father of the young woman,"
the verse spoke of "a young woman" written in full.
phrases.notes: Most times in this פרשה the word is written נער with no ה at the end. Here the ה is there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case of an orphan girl to a new limit on the fine: the age of the girl.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who falsely accuses a קטנה is פטור, learned from the full spelling of ״נערה״.

steps.title: Why would we need a spelling hint at all?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר אבא objects that the פסוק already obviously speaks of a נערה, since it calls for stoning and a קטנה cannot be punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר אבא challenged this. Are you saying the only reason is the full spelling, and without it we would have included a קטנה? But the פסוק says that if the accusation is true, they stone the girl. A קטנה is never punished. So the whole פרשה is obviously about a נערה already.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר אבא attacks how ריש לקיש learned his rule. The rule itself is not the target. He says ריש לקיש did not need the spelling to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the accusation is true, the girl is stoned. A קטנה cannot be punished, so this פרשה must be about a נערה no matter how the word is spelled. That makes the spelling hint useless for ריש לקיש's point.

keyTerms.meaning: Stoning, the punishment here if the accusation is true

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Abba challenged it:
Is the reason because "the young woman" is written regarding her,
so that if it were not so,
I would have said even a minor is included?!
But it is written:
"But if this matter was true,
signs of virginity were not found for the young woman.
Then they shall bring out the young woman
to the entrance of her father's house and stone her,"
and a minor is not subject to punishment!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source ריש לקיש used in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's use of the full spelling ״נערה״ to leave out a קטנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פרשה calls for stoning, and a קטנה cannot be punished. So the פרשה is clearly about a נערה, and the spelling hint adds nothing.

steps.title: Flipping the lesson: the short spelling includes a minor
steps.stepSummary: The full spelling here is a contrast. Everywhere the Torah writes ״נער״ without a ה, even a קטנה is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here the תורה wrote נערה in full because this פרשה really means a נערה. From that we learn that anywhere the תורה writes נער without the ה, even a קטנה is included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רב אחא בר אבא's point and changes what the spelling teaches. The lesson now looks outward, to every other place in the תורה where the word appears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full spelling is not needed to leave out a קטנה here, because stoning already does that. Instead it is a contrast: the full spelling is used only where a real נערה is meant. So the short spelling elsewhere covers a קטנה too, and leaves out only a בוגרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; brings in a new way of reading the source
Every place, anywhere in the תורה

steps.confusionAlert: The word ״נַעֲרָ״ is printed without a ה on purpose. It shows the short spelling, so it is not a typo.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a general rule for reading the תורה. Laws written with the short spelling ״נער״ can apply to a קטנה as well.

phrases.english: Rather: here it says "young woman" in full,
which shows that wherever it says "na'ara" without the heh,
even a minor is included in the meaning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 15 by changing what the full spelling teaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the source: the derivation is turned around.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The full spelling was thought to leave out a קטנה from this פרשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The full spelling marks where a real נערה is meant. The short spelling elsewhere includes even a קטנה.

steps.title: שילא begins listing three cases of an accused girl
steps.stepSummary: שילא teaches a ברייתא with three cases of a נערה, starting with witnesses who come after her wedding about something she did during אירוסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: שילא taught: There are three different cases about a נערה. The first is when witnesses come while she is already in her father-in-law's house and say she was unfaithful while she was still in her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא from שילא. It is setting up a list of three cases, and only the first case begins here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Her father-in-law's house" means after the wedding (נישואין). "Her father's house" means the time of אירוסין. The cases will differ by when the sin happened and when the witnesses came, and that decides her punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: Her father-in-law's house, meaning after the wedding

phrases.english: Sheila taught:
There are three categories regarding a young woman:
If witnesses came about her when she was in her father-in-law's house,
saying that she committed adultery in her father's house,
phrases.notes: Her father's house means while she was only engaged (אירוסין), before she moved in with her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא that sorts out the different cases of an accused נערה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three categories of an accused נערה. The first is when witnesses come after the wedding about adultery during אירוסין. Its ruling continues on the next amud.
